reading.body:
Ten frontier technology risks are being modelled for insurance before they are priced, spanning unaligned AI, post-quantum encryption gaps, autonomous fleets, brain interfaces, decentralized compute, neuromorphic hardware, synthetic biology, digital twins, synthetic media, and AI-designed compounds.

The common pattern is liability without loss history. Each entry names a coverage area where the failure mode is novel enough that insurers cannot rely on past claims, so they are building risk models before any established pricing exists. That includes systemic disruption from an unaligned frontier system, migration gaps in encryption, and drift between a digital twin and its physical plant.

Several entries sit directly on compute infrastructure. Decentralised compute networks are modelled because hardware security cannot be centrally assured, autonomous fleet liability shifts to cloud infrastructure when navigation is cloud controlled, and neuromorphic and optical hardware needs breakdown cover with no established failure statistics. Insurance modelling is therefore part of the path to deploying these architectures at scale.

The data does not show whether any of these products are actually offered, at what price, or with what exclusions. It also says nothing about power supply or physical building constraints, which are separate bottlenecks for AI scaling.
